precedence: recommendation; user requirements and project-owned instructions take precedence

entries.title: Architecture overview
entries.summary: Preserve project boundaries and dependency direction; do not impose a new architecture.
keyRules: Preserve the project's documented module boundaries and dependency direction.
Do not impose a new architecture on an existing project.

entries.title: Module design principles
entries.summary: Keep responsibilities cohesive and interfaces difficult to misuse.
keyRules: Keep module responsibilities cohesive and interfaces difficult to misuse.

entries.title: Module boundaries
entries.summary: Define ownership and cross-module access rules before implementation.
keyRules: Define module ownership and cross-module access before implementation.

entries.title: Dependency direction
entries.summary: Keep dependencies acyclic and respect public module APIs.
keyRules: Keep dependencies acyclic and respect public module APIs.

entries.title: Feature-sliced layers
entries.summary: Use only when the target project already adopts feature-sliced architecture.
keyRules: Use feature-sliced layers only when the project already adopts them.

entries.title: Naming
entries.summary: Use domain terms and existing naming conventions.
keyRules: Use domain terms and the project's existing naming conventions.

entries.title: Imports
entries.summary: Keep imports explicit and aligned with project module systems.
keyRules: Keep imports explicit and aligned with the project's module system.

entries.title: Error handling
entries.summary: Keep failures observable, scoped and free of leaked internals.
keyRules: Keep failures observable, scoped and free of leaked internals.

entries.title: TypeScript coding
entries.summary: Preserve strict typing and contain unsafe values at boundaries.
keyRules: Preserve strict typing and contain unsafe values at boundaries.

entries.title: Interface contracts
entries.summary: Design observable contracts, validation, failure modes and compatibility first.
keyRules: Define observable contracts, validation, failure modes and compatibility.
Design interfaces before implementation when the contract is still open.

entries.title: HTTP API design
entries.summary: Define schemas, authorization, errors, pagination and compatibility.
keyRules: Design resources, validation, errors and compatibility before implementation.

entries.title: HTTP API security
entries.summary: Enforce authentication, object authorization, limits, replay protection and safe errors.
keyRules: Authenticate and authorize every protected API operation on the server.
Validate untrusted input at the API boundary and avoid leaking internals.

entries.title: Database design
entries.summary: Keep invariants, constraints, indexing and compatibility explicit.
keyRules: Design schema ownership, constraints and query access before implementation.

entries.title: Database migrations
entries.summary: Use additive, reversible and data-safe migration sequencing.
keyRules: Make migrations ordered, reversible where practical and safe for existing data.

entries.title: PostgreSQL
entries.summary: Follow PostgreSQL-specific transaction, locking and migration constraints.
keyRules: Use PostgreSQL transactions, locking and migration semantics correctly.

entries.title: Cross-cutting security
entries.summary: Apply least privilege, secret hygiene and trust-boundary validation.
keyRules: Validate untrusted input at trust boundaries and authorize on the server.
Keep secrets out of source, logs, responses, client bundles and fixtures.

entries.title: Testing strategy
entries.summary: Choose tests by behavior and risk; keep them deterministic and independent.
keyRules: Choose tests by behavior and risk; keep them deterministic and independent.

entries.title: Unit testing
entries.summary: Test public behavior and edge cases without real network or clock dependencies.
keyRules: Test public behavior and edge cases without real network or clock dependencies.

entries.title: Component testing
entries.summary: Verify semantics, interactions, state changes and responsive behavior.
keyRules: Verify semantics, interactions, state changes and responsive behavior.

entries.title: Browser and visual testing
entries.summary: Cover critical journeys with stable fixtures and reviewed visual baselines.
keyRules: Cover critical journeys with stable fixtures and reviewed visual baselines.

entries.title: Python
entries.summary: Use explicit boundaries, safe deserialization, typed interfaces and project tooling.
keyRules: Use explicit boundaries, safe deserialization and type annotations at public interfaces.
Use context managers and catch specific exceptions at recovery points.

entries.title: Vue 3
entries.summary: Keep reactive ownership, cleanup, list keys and computed purity correct.
keyRules: Keep reactive ownership and computed purity clear; clean up watchers, timers and listeners.
Use stable list keys and confirm prop reactivity for the project's compiler version.

entries.title: TypeScript language
entries.summary: Preserve strictness, validate unknowns and contain any at boundaries.
keyRules: Preserve strictness, validate unknowns and contain any at boundaries.

entries.title: JavaScript
entries.summary: Use explicit module boundaries, safe async errors and project conventions.
keyRules: Use explicit module boundaries, safe async errors and project conventions.

entries.title: Go
entries.summary: Prefer clear errors, context propagation and bounded concurrency.
keyRules: Prefer clear errors, context propagation and bounded concurrency.

entries.title: Java
entries.summary: Keep boundaries explicit and use project-standard validation and error handling.
keyRules: Keep boundaries explicit and use project-standard validation and error handling.

entries.title: Rust
entries.summary: Contain unsafe code, keep ownership clear and handle fallible paths explicitly.
keyRules: Contain unsafe code, keep ownership clear and handle fallible paths explicitly.
